Many of the prehistoric and historic Indian sites found in Tracts
II and III, have been subjected to destruction over the years. Arrow
head hunters have removed surface evidence of potentially good and\nimportant sites, and other sites have been vandalized or disrupted as a
result of modern land uses.
It is difficult to estimate just how many sites will be uncovered and destroyed by mining operations. However, Westmoreland Resources has stated that great care will be exercised to protect known sites where possible. Further, when a sub-surface site is uncovered by mining machinery the work will be halted and an archaeologiat summoned to inspect the site. For example, a previously unknown site (24BH1728) was discovered in the area of the proposed coal handling facilities during the 1972 Tract III survey. Before the area was disturbed, the site was carefully excavated and artifacts salvaged.
Historic Sites
There are no significant historic sites in the area to be mined, although a number of existing ranch site and abandoned homesteads which will be removed may have local historic interest. Mining will not affect any sites currently listed on or eligible for federal or state historic registers (Westmoreland Resources, 1975 h).
CHANGES IN OWNERSHIP, USE AND PRODUCTIVITY OF THE LAND SURFACE
